posts.title: Mercado Bitcoin Assures Users Won’t Lose Funds Following $38M Security Breach
posts.titleVi: Mercado Bitcoin Assures Users Won’t Lose Funds Following $38M Security Breach
posts.summary: Mercado Bitcoin has assured customers they won’t lose any funds after the security incident that led it to suspend deposits and withdrawals on Monday. The Brazilian crypto exchange has now put the value of the assets involved at around $38 million.
posts.summaryVi: Mercado Bitcoin has assured customers they won’t lose any funds after the security incident that led it to suspend deposits and withdrawals on Monday. The Brazilian crypto exchange has now put the value of the assets involved at around $38 million.
posts.content:
Mercado Bitcoin has assured customers they won’t lose any funds after the security incident that led it to suspend deposits and withdrawals on Monday.

The Brazilian crypto exchange has now put the value of the assets involved at around $38 million. Meanwhile, it had already blocked $11 million in coordination with Tether, Circle, Paxos, BRL1, and Chainalysis.

In its latest update, Mercado Bitcoin said other amounts eligible for blocking have also been identified, and containment efforts are continuing. The statement comes after an incident identified in one of the company’s systems during the early hours of Monday. The exchange temporarily suspended access to services as a preventive measure to protect customer assets. It said services would resume once full security conditions were in place.

The initial scale of the incident was reported by blockchain security firm Hypernative, which said more than $40 million had moved out of wallets tied to Mercado Bitcoin overnight. The firm’s preliminary estimate covered transfers across at least 10 blockchains, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana and Tron. The exchange had previously said no customer data had leaked.

The first suspicious transfer was recorded at 2:15 UTC, while the largest movements took place between 6:19 and 6:53 UTC, when wallets linked to the exchange sent funds to newly created addresses. The transactions appeared to be ordinary signed transfers, meaning they were sent as though the source wallets had authorized them. Hypernative said it was still unclear how the attacker obtained the ability to sign those transactions.

The industry has had little breathing room, especially after the reported $6.3 billion Binance hack.

Meanwhile, ZachXBT flagged a separate suspected theft involving more than $133 million in withdrawals from centralized exchanges linked to an unnamed EU entity. The blockchain investigator identified an additional $27 million in withdrawals by the suspected illicit actor, which takes the total from the previously reported $106 million to more than $133 million.

The funds were withdrawn in USDC and USDT before the attacker began swapping USDC for ETH, routing transactions through instant exchanges such as WellWallet and Kyrrex, and converting funds into privacy-focused cryptocurrency XMR through Wagyu. The actor also bridged funds across multiple blockchains. ZachXBT said he was highly confident the activity was not linked to North Korea’s Lazarus Group, citing multiple laundering indicators.

He believes a large financial institution in Western Europe may have been exploited and suspects the incident is being covered up. ZachXBT also criticized the absence of a proper incident disclosure, while claiming that more than $30 million had already been laundered and could have been frozen by EU law enforcement.

Chayanika has been working as a financial journalist for seven years. A graduate in Political Science and Journalism, her interest lies in regulatory implications with a focus on technological evolution in the crypto realm.

posts.content:
Binance relied on AI to fight fraud before hackers exploited internal tool in $6 billion theft

Attackers exploited an internal AI system to reach wallet engineers, prompting the exchange to seek security partnerships with leading AI companies.

By Oluwapelumi Adejumo Senior Reporter • CryptoSlate

01 Hackers exploited Binance's internal AI tool to compromise wallet engineers before stealing $6.34 billion in cryptocurrency. 02 The breach exposed security weaknesses at an exchange that relied on more than 100 AI models. 03 Binance is seeking partnerships with leading AI firms and commissioning an independent security review, with key details of both initiatives undisclosed. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

Hackers exploited Binance's internal artificial intelligence tools to compromise engineers before stealing $6.34 billion in cryptocurrency, the exchange disclosed.

In its Nov. 3 security report , Binance said attackers used a compromised employee computer and an internal AI tool on Oct. 20 to take control of two engineers responsible for its wallet infrastructure.

The attackers subsequently obtained access to a container deployment permission token, which helped them penetrate the exchange's wallet-signing operations on Oct. 29 and initiate unauthorized transactions across several blockchain networks.

The disclosure puts AI at the center of one of the largest cryptocurrency thefts on record, adding to concerns about how increasingly connected AI systems can introduce new vulnerabilities into corporate infrastructure.

Binance's investigation does not establish that an AI model autonomously planned or executed the theft. Rather, the attackers exploited an internal AI tool as part of a broader campaign involving stolen credentials, compromised developer software, and social engineering.

In June, a Binance engineer downloaded a tampered software installer while attempting to install a popular AI coding tool. Binance detected the suspicious activity, replaced the device and rotated associated credentials, although information about the employee and colleagues had already been exposed.

In September, another engineer fell victim to a fake recruitment operation involving staged job interviews and a malicious coding assignment. The malware compromised the employee's computer and gave the attackers access, which they later used to move deeper into Binance's systems.

The FBI has attributed the broader attack to North Korea , whose hacking operations have increasingly targeted software developers and cryptocurrency businesses.

AI becomes a growing weapon in cyberattacks

The Binance incident follows months of warnings from cybersecurity researchers that artificial intelligence is expanding both hackers' capabilities and the systems available for exploitation.

In February, Google's Mandiant reported that North Korean hackers targeting the cryptocurrency industry had incorporated AI-assisted techniques into their operations.

The researchers documented an intrusion involving a fake video conference, malicious software, and a suspected AI-generated video impersonating a corporate executive. They could not independently confirm the deepfake in that particular incident but identified the group's use of AI tools for reconnaissance and social engineering.

By September, Google's Threat Intelligence Group reported that attackers were moving beyond using AI to generate malicious content toward automated operations that could execute multiple stages of an intrusion.

Related Reading Blockchain malware activity jumps 440% as AI lowers the barrier for North Korea and Iran-linked hackers

In one case, hackers compromised a cloud resource and organized an AI-assisted mass credential-harvesting campaign in less than six hours. Google also identified attackers attempting to manipulate AI coding assistants and security scanners during software supply-chain compromises.

The findings closely resemble one aspect of the Binance breach: developers and the AI-powered tools they depend on are becoming targets attackers use to reach sensitive systems.

Separately, AI developer Anthropic disclosed in September that criminals and suspected state-sponsored operators had used its Claude models to conduct reconnaissance , develop exploitation tools, and automate data theft.

Some operations involved AI agents carrying out multiple stages of an attack with limited human supervision, reducing the technical expertise and manpower traditionally required.

Binance turns to AI companies to strengthen security

The exchange is now seeking support from the same industry whose technologies were featured in the attack.

Binance said it is working to establish a security research fund and develop targeted initiatives with leading AI companies, blockchain industry participants and cybersecurity firms.

The proposed collaboration will focus on strengthening AI security in blockchain environments, although the exchange has not disclosed the fund's proposed size, participating companies or launch date.

It also plans to expand spending on AI-enabled threat detection, endpoint protection, developer-environment security and behavioral anomaly monitoring.

The exchange said it has already rebuilt the affected internal AI tool and wallet infrastructure, replaced compromised employee devices and strengthened access controls.

Binance has also commissioned an independent cybersecurity review to validate its investigation and identify additional safeguards.

The company said approximately $2.85 billion of the $6.34 billion in affected digital assets has been frozen or intercepted, while 98% of impacted token assets had been replenished as of Oct. 31.

The independent review has yet to establish the full extent of the weaknesses that allowed attackers to exploit the exchange's internal AI environment. Its findings will inform the security changes Binance plans to implement as it develops the proposed industry fund.

The exchange said it has already rebuilt the affected internal AI tool and wallet infrastructure, replaced compromised employee devices and strengthened access controls.

Binance has also commissioned an independent cybersecurity review to validate its investigation and identify additional safeguards.

The company said approximately $2.85 billion of the $6.34 billion in affected digital assets has been frozen or intercepted, while 98% of impacted token assets had been replenished as of Oct. 31.

The independent review has yet to establish the full extent of the weaknesses that allowed attackers to exploit the exchange's internal AI environment. Its findings will inform the security changes Binance plans to implement as it develops the proposed industry fund.

Written by Isabelle Castro staff writer Edited by Ana Paula Pereira staff editor Written by Isabelle Castro staff writer Edited by Ana Paula Pereira staff editor

SpaceX blocks tokenized stock listing on OKXICE despite offshore trading boom

Latest News Published Nov 3, 2026 SpaceX joined several other issuers objecting to OKXICE tokenized trading, months after crypto platforms offered tokens tied to its shares.

Just months after tokenized versions of SpaceX shares became one of the biggest drivers of onchain stock trading, the aerospace company is pushing back against plans to bring similar trading to US investors.

According to a Nov. 2 public notice from OKXICE, SpaceX has objected to the proposed listing of tokenized versions of its shares on the trading venue, a joint venture between crypto exchange OKX and New York Stock Exchange parent Intercontinental Exchange (ICE). The company now joins Tesla and Amazon among 56 companies objecting to the proposed listings.

Under the Securities and Exchange Commission’s five-year Innovation Exemption introduced in September, platforms such as OKXICE can offer trading in tokenized versions of US stocks without registering as national securities exchanges. But the framework also gives companies a say in the process: They have 30 days to object to the proposed trading of their shares tokenized by third parties, effectively keeping those tokens off the venue.

Tokenized stocks are blockchain-based representations of company shares that allow investors to gain exposure to traditional equities onchain, often around the clock. Depending on the structure, they can be backed by actual shares, although the rights granted to tokenholders may differ from those of traditional shareholders.

OKXICE co-chair and former New York Governor Andrew Cuomo told Cointelegraph on Oct. 20 that the venture expected more objections as companies avoided being the first to test the model.

SpaceX’s objection comes despite tokenized versions of its shares already trading on platforms outside the US, where they have attracted significant trading activity since the company’s June public offering.

Ahead of the SpaceX listing, Backpack Securities, a stock brokerage and tokenization platform, and crypto exchange Kraken, through its xStocks offering, both prepared tokenized versions of the aerospace company’s stock, each designed to be backed by actual shares. Backpack’s SPCX token went on to record $1.08 billion in onchain trading volume in June, while Kraken’s SPCXx token recorded $852 million.

Unlike Backpack and Kraken, OKXICE would open tokenized stock trading to US investors under the SEC’s new regulatory framework, potentially tapping into the world’s largest equity market by capitalization and expanding the investor base for tokenized securities.

Nasdaq warned issuers in September that they “must be cautious about their participation” in the venture, arguing that tokenized stock trading could fragment liquidity and undermine long-term shareholder value.

Despite the growing opposition, Cuomo said during an Oct. 30 press conference that as people see the benefits of tokenization, “you’ll see more and more companies participate.”

SpaceX chặn niêm yết cổ phiếu được token hóa trên OKXICE bất chấp sự bùng nổ giao dịch ở nước ngoài

Tin tức mới nhất được xuất bản vào ngày 3 tháng 11 năm 2026 SpaceX đã tham gia cùng một số tổ chức phát hành khác phản đối giao dịch mã thông báo OKXICE, vài tháng sau khi các nền tảng tiền điện tử cung cấp mã thông báo gắn liền với cổ phiếu của nó.

Chỉ vài tháng sau khi các phiên bản mã hóa của cổ phiếu SpaceX trở thành một trong những động lực lớn nhất của giao dịch chứng khoán trực tuyến, công ty hàng không vũ trụ này đang phản đối kế hoạch đưa giao dịch tương tự đến với các nhà đầu tư Hoa Kỳ.

Theo thông báo công khai ngày 2 tháng 11 từ OKXICE, SpaceX đã phản đối đề xuất niêm yết các phiên bản token hóa cổ phiếu của mình trên địa điểm giao dịch, một liên doanh giữa sàn giao dịch tiền điện tử OKX và Sàn giao dịch chứng khoán New York (ICE). Công ty hiện cùng với Tesla và Amazon trong số 56 công ty phản đối danh sách được đề xuất.

Theo Miễn trừ đổi mới 5 năm của Ủy ban Chứng khoán và Giao dịch được giới thiệu vào tháng 9, các nền tảng như OKXICE có thể cung cấp giao dịch bằng các phiên bản token hóa của chứng khoán Hoa Kỳ mà không cần đăng ký làm sàn giao dịch chứng khoán quốc gia. Nhưng khuôn khổ này cũng giúp các công ty có tiếng nói trong quá trình này: Họ có 30 ngày để phản đối đề xuất giao dịch cổ phiếu của họ được mã hóa bởi các bên thứ ba, giúp loại bỏ các mã thông báo đó khỏi địa điểm một cách hiệu quả.

Cổ phiếu được mã hóa là đại diện dựa trên blockchain của cổ phiếu công ty cho phép các nhà đầu tư tiếp cận với cổ phiếu truyền thống trên chuỗi, thường là suốt ngày đêm. Tùy thuộc vào cấu trúc, chúng có thể được hỗ trợ bằng cổ phiếu thực tế, mặc dù các quyền được cấp cho chủ sở hữu mã thông báo có thể khác với quyền của cổ đông truyền thống.

Đồng chủ tịch OKXICE và cựu Thống đốc New York Andrew Cuomo nói với Cointelegraph vào ngày 20 tháng 10 rằng liên doanh dự kiến ​​sẽ có nhiều phản đối hơn khi các công ty tránh trở thành người đầu tiên thử nghiệm mô hình.

Sự phản đối của SpaceX được đưa ra bất chấp các phiên bản mã hóa cổ phiếu của họ đã được giao dịch trên các nền tảng bên ngoài Hoa Kỳ, nơi chúng đã thu hút được hoạt động giao dịch đáng kể kể từ đợt phát hành cổ phiếu ra công chúng vào tháng 6 của công ty.

Trước khi SpaceX niêm yết, Backpack Securities, một nền tảng môi giới chứng khoán và token hóa cũng như sàn giao dịch tiền điện tử Kraken, thông qua dịch vụ xStocks, cả hai đều đã chuẩn bị các phiên bản token hóa cho cổ phiếu của công ty hàng không vũ trụ, mỗi phiên bản được thiết kế để được hỗ trợ bằng cổ phiếu thực tế. Mã thông báo SPCX của Backpack tiếp tục đạt kỷ lục 1,08 tỷ USD về khối lượng giao dịch trên chuỗi vào tháng 6, trong khi mã thông báo SPCXx của Kraken ghi nhận 852 triệu USD.

Không giống như Backpack và Kraken, OKXICE sẽ mở giao dịch cổ phiếu mã hóa cho các nhà đầu tư Hoa Kỳ theo khung pháp lý mới của SEC, có khả năng thâm nhập vào thị trường vốn lớn nhất thế giới bằng cách vốn hóa và mở rộng cơ sở nhà đầu tư cho chứng khoán mã hóa.Nasdaq đã cảnh báo các tổ chức phát hành vào tháng 9 rằng họ “phải thận trọng khi tham gia” vào liên doanh, cho rằng giao dịch cổ phiếu token hóa có thể làm giảm tính thanh khoản và làm suy yếu giá trị cổ đông dài hạn.

Bất chấp sự phản đối ngày càng tăng, Cuomo cho biết trong cuộc họp báo ngày 30 tháng 10 rằng khi mọi người nhìn thấy lợi ích của việc mã hóa, “bạn sẽ thấy ngày càng nhiều công ty tham gia”.

Cointelegraph cam kết cung cấp báo chí độc lập, chất lượng cao trong các ngành công nghiệp tiền điện tử, blockchain, AI và fintech.

Tất cả tin tức, đánh giá và phân tích đều được sản xuất với sự độc lập và chính trực hoàn toàn về mặt báo chí. Để biết thêm chi tiết về các tiêu chuẩn và quy trình của chúng tôi, vui lòng đọc Chính sách biên tập của chúng tôi.

posts.content:
Bitcoin investors could pay the price as the Federal Reserve tightens bank lending rules

The Fed's Nov. 2 survey shows tougher approvals alongside stronger nonbank demand, with no evidence of forced Bitcoin sales.

By Gino Matos Reporter • CryptoSlate

01 Domestic banks reported tighter standards across all five nonbank borrower categories in the Fed's Nov. 2 survey. 02 Business-lender standards showed 22% of net tightening, while most responding banks left approvals unchanged. 03 Wider credit spreads signal financing pressure, while an older broad index tempers claims of a systemic squeeze reaching Bitcoin. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

Banks tightened loan approval standards for nonbank financial firms while reporting stronger demand from business lenders and private-equity funds, according to the Federal Reserve's Nov. 2 lending survey.

That combination points to a financing constraint that could limit investors' appetite for Bitcoin beyond changes in the Fed's policy rate.

For business lenders, classified as business credit intermediaries in the survey, 12 of 50 responding domestic banks tightened standards , one eased, and 37 left them unchanged. The response table shows 24% tightening versus 2% easing, for a net tightening of 22%.

The October Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey covers the preceding three months, generally the third quarter. Responses were due Oct. 5, well before the late-October spread widening.

Domestic banks reported net tightening across all five nonbank borrower categories surveyed. They most often cited a less favorable or more uncertain economic outlook and deterioration in borrowers' financial strength.

At the same time, banks reported stronger demand from business credit intermediaries and private-equity funds in a question measuring funds actually disbursed.

Thanks for signing up to The Catalyst. Look out for your first daily email. If you already receive it, you’re all set.

Among banks reporting stronger nonbank demand, common reasons included working-capital or liquidity needs, refinancing, and financial investment opportunities. Banks can become more selective even as borrowers seek financing for both cash needs and investments.

A minority of banks tightened business-lender standards, producing a 22-point net balance. The survey and market indicators describe different periods.

Approval tightening is real, but neither its bank-share measure nor these mismatched dates establishes Bitcoin selling.

The Federal Reserve's October SLOOS, released November 2, reports that domestic banks tightened standards on net across all five queried nonbank financial borrower categories during the prior quarter, generally Q3 2026. Fed SLOOS November 2 release For business credit intermediaries, 12 of 50 responding domestic banks tightened standards, one eased and 37 left them unchanged: 24% minus 2% yields net tightening of 22 percentage points. Fed SLOOS domestic-bank Table 1 Fed SLOOS domestic-bank Table 1 The survey was sent September 21 and responses were due October 5; 61 domestic banks and 18 US branches and agencies of foreign banks responded. Fed SLOOS November 2 release The ICE BofA US High Yield Index option-adjusted spread available on FRED rose from 3.14% on October 28 to 3.44% on October 30, a 30-basis-point widening; October 30 was the latest observation in the November 3 morning retrieval. ICE high-yield spread via FRED The Chicago Fed National Financial Conditions Index stood at -0.487 for the week ending October 23, the latest observation available in the November 3 morning retrieval; negative readings indicate conditions looser than average. Chicago Fed NFCI via FRED Survey covers Q3, with responses due Oct. 5. NFCI describes the week ending Oct. 23; spreads compare Oct. 28 and 30, the latest data exposed Nov. 3 morning. These separate measures do not establish Bitcoin selling.

Method: One square represents one of 50 banks answering Q29B: 12 tightened, 37 unchanged, 1 eased. Verified arithmetic: 12/50=24%, 1/50=2%, and (12−1)/50=22 percentage points net. Spread change: (3.44−3.14)×100=30 basis points. Date positions are schematic, not a time-proportional or causal scale.

Approval standards determine access to credit, so financing can become harder to obtain without a new policy-rate increase. The Fed held its target range at 3.75% to 4% on Oct. 28 , a separate decision from the earlier lending conditions captured by the survey.

If financing becomes harder to secure while liquidity needs rise, investors may have less capacity or willingness to hold risky assets. A 2023 IMF working paper found that US monetary tightening historically reduced a common crypto-price factor through that channel.

Related Reading Bitcoin faces an inflation warning beneath steady US consumer sentiment

The ICE BofA US high-yield option-adjusted spread rose from 3.14% on Oct. 28 to 3.44% on Oct. 30, a widening of 30 basis points.

The Chicago Fed National Financial Conditions Index was -0.487 for the week ending Oct. 23, indicating conditions looser than average.

A stronger signal of spillover would be continued widening in credit premiums alongside weakening Bitcoin demand , while narrowing spreads and resilient demand would weaken that case. For now, the survey shows a financing constraint worth watching.

posts.title: NEAR Governance Approves Major Supply Cut – But Token Slides 7%
posts.titleVi: NEAR Governance Approves Major Supply Cut – But Token Slides 7%
posts.summary: A proposal to gradually lower NEAR Protocol’s maximum annual token issuance from 2.5% to 1.6% over 24 months has secured approval from the network’s House of Stake governance body.
posts.summaryVi: A proposal to gradually lower NEAR Protocol’s maximum annual token issuance from 2.5% to 1.6% over 24 months has secured approval from the network’s House of Stake governance body.
posts.content:
A proposal to gradually lower NEAR Protocol’s maximum annual token issuance from 2.5% to 1.6% over 24 months has secured approval from the network’s House of Stake governance body.

The measure, outlined under HSP-029, aims to slow supply growth and limit long-term token dilution while preserving the existing reward structure. It retains the current allocation of newly issued tokens. 90% goes to staking participants, and the remaining 10% is directed to the protocol treasury.

Rather than introducing a new emissions framework or changing validator reward distribution, the measure focuses on adjusting a single protocol parameter.

The reduction will be introduced gradually across network epochs. The issuance ceiling will decline by approximately 3.75 basis points each month until it reaches the 1.6% target. According to estimates in the proposal, the revised schedule could prevent around 11.8 million NEAR from entering circulation over the first two years, with the cumulative reduction reaching 66.1 million over six years. This would leave the network’s supply approximately 4.36% lower than under the existing issuance model.

The change is also expected to affect staking returns. Based on the network’s September participation figures, gross staking yield is projected to fall from 5.268% to 3.372% once the new issuance rate is fully implemented.

The move comes amidst several discussions within the NEAR ecosystem about how to improve token economics without introducing discretionary funding mechanisms. Earlier proposals involving a treasury-backed fund raised concerns about placing validator support and capital allocation under human decision-making rather than predictable protocol rules. HSP-029 instead opts for a scheduled adjustment that requires no new administrator, price oracle, or spending program.

The change will not take effect immediately following the vote. It still requires a Security Council review, ratification, and a 90-day waiting period before validators adopt the necessary upgrade. Once implemented, the lower issuance rate will be introduced gradually over 24 months, while the existing token distribution remains unchanged.

Rather than introducing a new emissions framework or changing validator reward distribution, the measure focuses on adjusting a single protocol parameter.

The reduction will be introduced gradually across network epochs. The issuance ceiling will decline by approximately 3.75 basis points each month until it reaches the 1.6% target. Written by Nate Kostar staff writer Edited by Ana Paula Pereira staff editor Written by Nate Kostar staff writer Edited by Ana Paula Pereira staff editor

CFTC clears stock perpetual futures for trading on US exchanges

Latest News Published Nov 3, 2026 US regulators are opening the door to stock-based perpetual futures, extending a popular crypto trading product into traditional markets amid ongoing legal disputes.

Perpetual futures contracts tied to individual stocks can begin trading on regulated US exchanges for the first time, according to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), extending a derivatives product popularized in cryptocurrency markets into traditional equities.

CFTC Chairman Michael Selig said in a Tuesday statement that the contracts were deemed approved under CFTC Regulation 40.3 and could be offered on exchanges registered with both the CFTC and Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to trade security futures products.

Selig said bringing the products into regulated US markets would allow American traders to access perpetual futures under US regulatory safeguards rather than being “forced to turn to offshore, and often unregulated, venues.”

Perpetual futures allow traders to take positions on an asset’s price without owning the underlying asset or facing an expiration date. Crypto exchange BitMEX helped popularize the instruments, commonly referred to as perps, in 2016.

CFTC announces approval of equity perpetual futures trading. Source: CFTC

The announcement follows a wave of regulatory filings in September, when Coinbase, Kalshi and Kraken parent Payward, through its Bitnomial exchange, sought approval to offer perpetual futures tied to individual US stocks. OG.com joined the push days later, proposing contracts that could trade around the clock on weekdays.

The filings followed the CFTC’s May approval of Bitcoin perpetual futures contracts for Kalshi and separate regulatory relief allowing Coinbase to provide access to certain cryptocurrency perpetual futures listed on an affiliated foreign exchange.

Selig did not identify which exchanges would offer the contracts or provide a timeline for when trading would begin.

Related: CFTC sues Utah to block action against prediction markets

The announcement also comes nearly three months after President Donald Trump said the CFTC was working to bring Hyperliquid, a decentralized crypto exchange best known for its perpetual futures trading, into the US in a “fully compliant and legal fashion.”

Trump made the remarks during an Aug. 19 White House event . At the time, neither the CFTC nor Hyperliquid had announced a formal plan for bringing the platform to US markets.

However, the CFTC’s approach to perpetual futures has faced legal opposition. In June, CME Group’s Chicago Mercantile Exchange sued the regulator over its approval of cryptocurrency perpetual futures, arguing that the contracts should be regulated as swaps rather than futures and that the agency had exceeded its authority. The distinction matters because swaps are subject to different regulatory requirements, potentially including stricter reporting, margin and registration rules, while futures can trade under the existing futures exchange framework.

The CFTC moved to dismiss the lawsuit in September, arguing that CME lacked standing because it had not demonstrated financial harm and could list similar contracts itself.

Meanwhile, the Capital Markets Alliance, a coalition that includes Cboe, Citadel Securities and Healthy Markets, filed a lawsuit Tuesday afternoon seeking to overturn the CFTC’s approval.

The group argues that the contracts are security-based swaps under the SEC’s jurisdiction and that the CFTC violated the Administrative Procedure Act by failing to adequately explain its decision or consider the potential impact on investors. The lawsuit also seeks to prevent the approvals from taking effect while the case proceeds.

Written by Isabelle Castro staff writer Edited by Ana Paula Pereira staff editor Written by Isabelle Castro staff writer Edited by Ana Paula Pereira staff editor

US midterms: Prediction markets favor Democrats in key crypto races

Latest News Published Nov 3, 2026 Kalshi and Polymarket price a 75% chance of a Democratic sweep, days after markets misjudged Brazil’s runoff.

Update (Nov. 3 at 10:32 p.m. UTC): This article has been updated to include comments from Talos.

As Americans across the country head to the polls for the US midterm elections Tuesday, prediction market traders have spent months wagering on the outcome. According to an analysis by The Washington Post, nearly $1.9 billion in election-related contracts had traded on Kalshi and Polymarket as of Monday, marking record trading activity for a midterm election cycle.

Markets on both platforms favor Democrats winning control of Congress, with a Democratic sweep priced at 75% on Kalshi and 75.5% on Polymarket as of 4:30 pm UTC. Kalshi traders gave Democrats a 93% chance of taking the House and a 75% chance of winning the Senate, while Polymarket priced those outcomes at 94.5% and 75.5% , respectively.

The vote comes nine days after prediction markets failed to anticipate the outcome of Brazil’s presidential election, with Flávio Bolsonaro favored at roughly 80% the day before incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won the runoff. Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour reportedly cautioned that “a 5% probability doesn’t mean it won’t happen,” according to CNBC.

For the crypto industry, a shift in congressional control could reshape the prospects for long-awaited regulatory clarity.

A key race for crypto has centered on the Senate seat in Ohio, where Defend American Jobs, part of the Fairshake super PAC network, allocated 54% of its total expenses. According to the official website, $36.9 million was spent on supporting Senator Jon Husted and $19.7 million opposing the staunch crypto critic, Democrat Sherrod Brown. Fairshake spent $40 million to help unseat Brown in 2024.

However, the flood of spending may be to no avail, with traders expecting a win for Brown. The Kalshi market for the race predicted a 72% chance for a Brown win and 72.5% on Polymarket, both in line with a final New York Times/Siena poll that had him ahead 49% to 44%.

A Brown victory could complicate the crypto industry’s legislative agenda, particularly if Democrats regain control of the Senate. Analysts have identified him as a potential chairman of the Senate Agriculture Committee, which oversees the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, although the leadership position remains uncertain.

Related: From Uptober to Hacktober: Are Bitcoin’s seasonal patterns becoming obsolete?

In Maine, however, a Democratic win predicted by traders could help the crypto industry expand its influence in Washington. Republican Senator Susan Collins was one of four Republicans who voted against advancing the CLARITY Act in September, stalling the bill in the Senate.

Kalshi gives Democrat Troy Jackson a 71% chance of unseating her, while Polymarket puts his chances at 71.5% , broadly in line with New York Times polls conducted in October that had Jackson ahead by two percentage points. Advocacy group Stand with Crypto rates Jackson as strongly supportive of crypto, potentially giving the industry another ally in the Senate should he win.

Although many prediction markets are broadly in line with polling results, traders have made clearer calls in three states where polls show close races.

In Alaska, Kalshi gives Democrat Mary Peltola a 71% chance of defeating Republican Senator Dan Sullivan, even though the final New York Times/Siena poll had her ahead by just two percentage points, 48% to 46%. Both candidates have expressed strong support for crypto, according to Stand With Crypto.

In South Carolina, where the candidates were tied at 48% in the New York Times/Siena poll, Kalshi gives Republican Senator Darline Graham, a crypto supporter, a 71% chance of defeating Democrat Annie Andrews.

Iowa remains a toss-up on both platforms, with Democrat Josh Turek overtaking Republican Representative Ashley Hinson on Polymarket at 52% , after months of Hinson being favored to win.

In other key races, prediction markets are broadly in line with the polls. In Michigan, Kalshi gives Democrat Abdul El-Sayed a 79% chance of defeating Republican Mike Rogers. Kalshi also gives Democrat James Talarico a 71% chance of defeating Republican Ken Paxton in Texas, while the final New York Times/Siena poll had Talarico ahead 50% to 43%. A Paxton loss would be a setback for the Digital Freedom Fund, a super PAC backed by Gemini’s co-founders Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss that spent more than $81,000 supporting his campaign. However, Talarico has also expressed support for the crypto industry.

Related: What’s at stake for crypto as the US votes in the 2026 midterms?

Despite the markets leaning towards a Democrat win in both the House and Senate, researchers from Talos have pointed to thin liquidity behind the contracts. According to Talos’ head of research, Kelly Ye, as of 11:30 am ET, just $300,000 of selling would have pushed Kalshi’s Democrats-win-Senate contract down ten points.

The median trade on the markets came in at around $10, with a few large-ticket trades making up the majority of the liquidity behind the contracts.

“As midterm results come in tonight, prediction markets will reprice quickly, but those prices are only as good as the liquidity behind them,” she said in a statement sent to Cointelegraph.

“Whatever happens tonight, one result won’t tell you whether these markets are accurate. Across many settled contracts, outcomes have broadly tracked prices.”

Markets are also starting to look beyond today’s vote to the political and economic landscape following a potential Democratic sweep of Congress. Polymarket’s conditional markets suggest traders are pricing in a higher risk of recession under Democratic control of both chambers, with the implied probability of a US recession by the end of 2027 at 35% if Democrats sweep and 19% if they do not, as of 4:50 pm UTC.

posts.content:
After a rough year (so far), the cryptocurrency community expected October to bring some relief and deliver substantial gains for certain digital assets. After all, it is among the strongest months for the market, hence its nickname “Uptober.” However, the period failed to meet expectations and ended with the $6.3 billion Binance hack, which suppressed the prices of numerous cryptocurrencies.

Attention has shifted to November, which features a busy calendar of economic and political developments that may drive additional market turbulence. Curious what AI had to say, we asked three of the most widely used chatbots which three cryptocurrencies deserve a $1,000 investment in November. We should add a vital disclaimer: this is not financial advice, but simply the opinion and analysis of some AI platforms. Here are their interesting answers.

OpenAI’s platform said allocating $1K each to Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), and Solana (SOL) seems most reasonable for November. The primary cryptocurrency is its first choice because the investment case there is “relatively straightforward: limited supply, established institutional access, and demand from investors seeking exposure to a scarce digital asset.”

ChatGPT said BTC’s bull case this month depends on a shift in the economic backdrop. It highlighted key events such as the US employment report on November 6, followed by CPI data scheduled for next week, saying they could reshape interest-rate expectations.

“If hiring cools without suggesting a recession, and inflation comes in softer than expected, investors could become more willing to buy risk assets. That would give Bitcoin a potential catalyst for recovery after October’s weakness,” it stated.

The platform’s second pick is ETH, calling it “a bet on blockchain infrastructure.” According to ChatGPT, the largest altcoin could benefit if a potential BTC recovery encourages investors to take more risk across major cryptocurrencies.

“The argument for putting $1,000 into ETH would be that improving sentiment could bring buyers back to an asset with established uses in transaction fees and staking – but that is a conditional recovery thesis, not a confirmed November event,” it added.

The platform said its third contender, SOL, has “the most concrete event” of the three: Breakpoint, scheduled for November 15-17 in London. The conference will focus on institutional adoption, payments, stablecoins, and tokenized assets. According to ChatGPT, it could create an opportunity for announcements that could positively impact the price.

Perplexity and Google’s Gemini shared quite different theories from ChatGPT. The former said its top pick for a $1K investment in November is Ripple’s XRP and explained why:

“XRP could spike in November because its spot ETFs have posted seven straight months of net inflows while institutional adoption expanded – BNY corporate payments, Standard Chartered custody, Ripple Bank approval, and RLUSD support – so renewed ETF demand or a favorable regulatory decision could trigger a sharp rebound from its oversold October decline.”

Perplexity’s second choice is Chainlink (LINK). It argued its price could rise in the coming weeks because major banks and financial firms are increasingly using its technology to connect and tokenize real-world assets, which could drive fresh demand for the coin.

The AI-powered chatbot placed Avalanche (AVAX) third, describing it as “the higher-beta ecosystem bet.” It claimed it has more upside potential but also more execution and competition risk.

Gemini also selected LINK and XRP as two of the three cryptocurrencies it believes could be worthwhile $1,000 investments in November. Its third pick was the rather surprising Ondo Finance (ONDO).

“Investing $1,000 in ONDO in November gives you direct exposure to Real-World Asset (RWA) tokenization, as traditional finance giants like BlackRock increasingly move Treasuries and equities on-chain,” it concluded.

Dimitar got interested in cryptocurrencies back in 2018 amid the prolonged bear market. His biggest passion in the field is Bitcoin and he was fascinated with its journey. With a flair for producing high-quality content, he started covering the cryptocurrency space in late 2018. His hobby is football.

posts.summaryVi: The CFTC cleared perpetual futures on individual stocks to trade on registered U.S. exchanges for the first time, bringing the expiration-free, leveraged instrument long popular in crypto to traditional equities.
posts.content:
The CFTC cleared perpetual futures on individual stocks to trade on registered U.S. exchanges for the first time, bringing the expiration-free, leveraged instrument long popular in crypto to traditional equities.

Chairman Michael Selig framed it as part of his push to “onshore” perpetual products, building on the agency’s earlier approval of Bitcoin perps for Kalshi.

The contracts fall under joint CFTC-SEC oversight via a March memorandum of understanding.

posts.content:
Binance says thinly traded tokens are delaying full replacement of stolen assets

Binance attributes its last reported 5% replenishment gap to less-liquid assets, while its November 3 withdrawal plan reopens routes progressively.

By Liam 'Akiba' Wright Editor-in-Chief • CryptoSlate

01 Binance's November 3 plan calls for withdrawals to reopen progressively as each asset-network pair clears security checks. 02 The 95% replenishment figure was reported November 1 and repeated November 2; remaining tokens are harder to source. 03 Binance says its completed reserve proof covers ten tokens at an Oct. 31 snapshot; a broader snapshot is planned for Nov. 4. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

Binance said in its Nov. 2 recovery update that less-liquid tokens were slowing the replacement of stolen assets. It put the outstanding replenishment at approximately 5% of the impacted amount, while a separate withdrawal phase was scheduled for Nov. 3.

The new phase was scheduled to begin at 04:00 UTC. In Binance's Nov. 3 update , the exchange said availability would expand progressively as security and readiness checks were completed for individual assets and networks.

Together, the disclosures explain why a commitment to cover stolen funds can coexist with unfinished recovery. Funding the purchases, obtaining the specific tokens and restoring the routes through which customers withdraw them are separate tasks.

Binance recovery has separate checkpoints

The replenishment percentage, dated reserve proof and asset-network reopening answer different questions.

REPLENISHMENT · LAST REPORTED NOV. 2 ~95% of the impacted amount ~5% outstanding Less-liquid tokens outside the named ten Market / OTC purchases + industry partners Nov. 1 figure repeated Nov. 2. This is a replenishment measure. REPLENISHMENT Nov. 1 figure · repeated Nov. 2 ~95% of the impacted amount ~5% outstanding Less-liquid tokens outside the named ten Market / OTC + industry partners

Compare the other recovery milestones Dated reserve proof Withdrawal routes Binance said proof for ten tokens at the October 31 snapshot was complete on November 2. This concerns backing at that snapshot.

SNAPSHOT · OCT. 31, 00:00 UTC BTC ETH USDT BNB SOL USDC XRP USD1 RLUSD ZEC Proof complete Nov. 2 Ten named tokens Binance says users can verify minimum 1:1 backing at that snapshot. SNAPSHOT · OCT. 31 00:00 UTC · ten named tokens BTC ETH USDT BNB SOL USDC XRP USD1 RLUSD ZEC Proof complete Nov. 2 Binance says minimum 1:1 backing at the dated snapshot.

The November 3 plan reopens asset-network pairs progressively after security checks. These examples do not establish current availability.

NOV. 3 PLAN · PROGRESSIVE REOPENING FROM 04:00 UTC TOKEN CHECK EACH PAIR NETWORK RLUSD USDC ? Ethereum ? XRP ? Sui ? = live status not established here. Check each planned pair after security checks. NOV. 3 · PROGRESSIVE ROLLOUT Planned from 04:00 UTC TOKEN CHECK NETWORK RLUSD ? Ethereum RLUSD ? XRP USDC ? Sui ? = live status not established here. Security checks apply to each pair.

A replenishment percentage does not establish that a particular withdrawal route is available.

Binance's statements are attributed reporting. The denominator's valuation basis is unspecified. No live route status or unreplenished token identity is established; the October 31 proof concerns ten named tokens.

Binance Recovery Update #6, Nov. 3 Binance Recovery Update #4, Nov. 1 Binance Recovery Update #5, Nov. 2 Supporting facts

Binance announced a further progressive withdrawal rollout beginning at 04:00 UTC on November 3, with listed assets becoming available as security and readiness checks are completed rather than all at once. [1] Binance's November 3 update says it is restoring each network-asset pair after security checks, prioritizing tokens using demand over the past week, and adding more assets as they become ready. [1] Binance reported on November 1 that it had covered approximately 95% of the impacted amount and repeated that figure on November 2. [2] [3] Binance said the outstanding approximately 5% of the impacted amount comprised tokens outside BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB, SOL, USDC, XRP, USD1, RLUSD and ZEC, and that these less-liquid assets take longer to source at the required scale. [3] Binance said it was continuing to acquire the remaining affected assets through market and over-the-counter channels and working with industry partners on the acquisitions. [2] [3] Binance said on November 2 that the zero-knowledge proof for its October 31, 00:00 UTC reserve snapshot was complete and users holding the ten named tokens could verify at least one-for-one backing. [3] Binance's ten-token snapshot and associated proof concern a specified asset set at October 31, 00:00 UTC; the withdrawal rollout separately concerns asset-network pairs and security readiness. [3] [1] Binance's November 3 planned-withdrawal table includes RLUSD on the Ethereum and XRP networks and USDC on Sui, but the announcement does not establish that all those routes are currently available. [1] Binance advised users to check the withdrawal page for their chosen asset and network or its network-status page, and warned that rollout traffic could cause delays or longer processing times. [1] Method

Source-bound comparison of Binance's disclosures. The approximate 95/5 bar represents the stated shares of the impacted amount, not token counts, dollars or withdrawal routes. Named pairs are examples from the planned November 3 table.

Binance's statements are attributed reporting. The denominator's valuation basis is unspecified. No live route status or unreplenished token identity is established; the October 31 proof concerns ten named tokens.

Related Reading Tracked Binance wallets record $2.5 billion in outflows as withdrawals reopen after hack

Binance reported approximately 95% replenishment of the impacted amount in its Nov. 1 recovery update . It repeated that figure on Nov. 2, attributing the outstanding portion to tokens outside the ten assets it said were fully backed: BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB, SOL, USDC, XRP, USD1, RLUSD and ZEC.

The exchange said the remaining assets were less liquid and took longer to source in the required quantities. It described continued purchases through market and over-the-counter channels, alongside work with industry partners to finish the acquisitions.

In its Oct. 31 update , Binance identified corporate treasury, a planned partial deployment of its Secure Asset Fund for Users and a portion of its futures insurance resources as recovery funding sources.

Related Reading CZ asks Musk to stop trolling, saying ‘our’ SpaceX shares top $1 billion

The percentage also has a narrower meaning than a general recovery score. Binance describes the denominator as the impacted amount. It does not specify the valuation basis in those disclosures, so the remaining 5% cannot safely be converted into a dollar shortfall. Nor does 95% describe the proportion of tokens or withdrawal routes restored.

Binance's Nov. 2 update said the zero-knowledge proof for its Oct. 31, 00:00 UTC reserve snapshot was complete. It said holders of the ten named tokens could independently verify that their balances were backed at least one-for-one.

The proof concerns a defined set of assets at a dated snapshot. Backing at that snapshot does not establish present availability of every withdrawal route.

Related Reading Binance can cut a winning Bitcoin hedge even when customer assets are backed

The latest withdrawal table illustrates why the network matters alongside the token. It includes RLUSD on Ethereum and XRP, and USDC on Sui, among routes planned for progressive reopening. Those entries identify the scope of the rollout, not which tokens remain unreplenished or whether each route is currently operational.

Binance said it was prioritizing tokens according to demand over the preceding week and restoring each network-asset pair after security checks.

For holders, the immediate check is the chosen asset and network. Binance directed users to its withdrawal page or network-status page to confirm availability, and warned that rollout traffic could cause temporary delays or longer processing times.

A separate transparency milestone is still ahead. Binance said it planned a Nov. 4 reserve snapshot covering more tokens, followed by proof generation estimated to take approximately 40 to 50 hours.

Binance reiterated that it would bear the financial impact of the stolen funds rather than pass losses on to users.

Crypto spent $55 million defending a senator who already backed CLARITY

One of crypto's most expensive election bets is playing out in Ohio, where winning could leave the industry's biggest problem in Washington untouched.

By Andjela Radmilac Senior Analyst • CryptoSlate

01 Crypto-backed Defend American Jobs spent more than $55 million supporting Husted and opposing Brown in Ohio. 02 Husted already voted to advance the CLARITY Act, which failed to reach the Senate's 60-vote threshold. 03 Tuesday's election could change Senate control without resolving the bill's disagreements. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

Defend American Jobs, a crypto-backed political group, spent more than $55 million supporting Republican Jon Husted and opposing Sherrod Brown in Ohio between Sept. 21 and Oct. 26, according to Americans for Financial Reform. Husted had already voted to advance the CLARITY Act.

Americans vote today, Nov. 3, in midterm elections that will determine control of Congress for the next two years. Republicans currently control both chambers.

Congress has to agree on crypto legislation, which means winning over enough lawmakers in both parties to get it passed.

The midterms will shape committee leadership, hearings and the path to a vote. Presidents appoint regulators and set enforcement priorities, but a later administration can change those policies.

Crypto-backed groups have poured money into congressional races , often backing candidates based on their crypto positions rather than their party.

Fairshake and its affiliated groups have become some of the biggest spenders in American politics, with a Reuters analysis estimating that crypto groups had spent roughly $176 million across more than 100 races by late October.

Ohio has become a major focus of that strategy.

Husted already voted in September to advance the CLARITY Act, a major proposal intended to establish clearer federal rules for crypto. The bill failed to clear a 60-vote Senate hurdle , leaving its supporters short of the backing needed to move forward. Brown, meanwhile, wasn't even in the Senate when that happened, having lost his previous seat in 2024 before launching a comeback campaign against Husted for Ohio's other Senate seat.

Keeping Husted in Washington would protect a vote the industry already has, while defeating Brown would prevent a prominent crypto critic from returning to Congress. Both outcomes would be politically valuable, especially with Senate control potentially at stake, but neither will resolve the disagreements that stopped the legislation in September.

That's because lawmakers are still fighting over stablecoin rewards, banking risks and the protections customers should receive when crypto companies handle their money, and the industry's expensive election campaign can't settle those disputes on its own.

Republicans currently hold 53 seats , so even a united Republican caucus would need support from outside the party to reach the 60-vote threshold used in September.

Susan Collins, Josh Hawley, and Jerry Moran all voted against moving ahead . Thom Tillis recorded a no as well, but did so to preserve the option of asking the Senate to reconsider , a procedural step that would allow another attempt rather than an expression of opposition to the bill itself.

Collins wanted further study of whether community banks and credit unions could lose deposits used to support “loans for mortgages, small businesses, and other family needs.” The dispute centers partly on stablecoin rewards. Crypto platforms offer rewards to customers who keep stablecoins in an account, giving those customers another reason to leave their money there, so banks see those offers as competition for money that might otherwise sit in a deposit account. Banking groups argue that losing those deposits could make it harder to fund lending , and they have pushed lawmakers to restrict rewards that work like interest.

The September proposal would restrict payments by third parties, such as exchanges , when those payments function like interest on bank deposits. It would still allow rewards tied to transactions or activity, which draws a distinction between paying someone to leave a balance untouched and rewarding them for actually using it.

Banking associations argue that the proposed distinction leaves ways to keep paying what is effectively interest , even when the payment is described or structured differently.

Under the September draft, Treasury could impose further restrictions if stablecoin yield caused substantial harm to community-bank deposits within 18 months of enactment. The sponsors presented that provision as protection for smaller banks and the businesses that rely on them.

Banking groups objected that waiting until significant damage had occurred would make the protection come too late. Their response called for tighter restrictions in the legislation itself , rather than relying on regulators to act after deposits had already moved.

Nevada Democrat Catherine Cortez Masto raised a different set of objections, saying the September version left unresolved problems involving illicit finance, prediction markets, and ethics . She supported the separate GENIUS stablecoin legislation, but said this proposal didn't do enough to help law enforcement address crypto crime or resolve concerns about political conflicts.

The sponsors said they incorporated 126 substantive changes requested by Democrats and revised the restrictions governing public officials’ crypto interests. Cortez Masto’s response was that important problems remained and that Republican Senate leaders had ended negotiations before they were resolved.

Those objections would still need answers after a Husted victory, unless the sponsors could find enough support elsewhere.

Even after an agreement in the Senate, the House would have to approve the same legislative text before it could go to the president. Democrats could ask for different terms from those accepted by the current chamber if they won a House majority, including in a scenario where Republicans held the Senate.

Congress can also act after the election and before its current term ends on Jan. 3, 2027 . That period gives lawmakers another opportunity to negotiate.

Bills that have not become law by the end of a Congress don't carry over automatically . The legislation would need to be introduced again and work through the process, leaving the newly elected House and Senate to decide which parts of the September proposal they were willing to keep.

posts.titleVi: 7,934 New XRP Wallets in One Day: Network Activity Defies Sunday Slowdown
posts.summary: XRP network growth appears to have picked up pace even as its price hovers near $1.25. Santiment found that 7,934 new wallets were created on November 1st, which happens to be the sixth-highest daily total of 2026.
posts.summaryVi: XRP network growth appears to have picked up pace even as its price hovers near $1.25. Santiment found that 7,934 new wallets were created on November 1st, which happens to be the sixth-highest daily total of 2026.
posts.content:
XRP network growth appears to have picked up pace even as its price hovers near $1.25. Santiment found that 7,934 new wallets were created on November 1st, which happens to be the sixth-highest daily total of 2026.

That’s notable, especially since Sundays are usually quieter for crypto network activity.

The surge follows a busy week for XRP and came just after the Binance hack, which may have pushed more users toward self-custody and fresh wallets. Santiment said that strong network growth suggests usage is improving while price remains under pressure. The immediate pivot is $1.25, and $1.30 is the first level that would confirm stronger momentum.

If daily new-wallet growth stays above roughly 4,000 and XRP reclaims $1.30, the setup looks more constructive. On the other hand, a drop below $1.20 and growth under 3,000 would weaken that signal.

CryptoPotato recently reported that XRP whale outflows on Binance also surged nearly three times the September 2022 reading. These outflows could ease near-term selling pressure.

XRP and other top caps such as Bitcoin and Ethereum have already been witnessing weakening sentiment for nearly two months. The Binance hack further accelerated the downfall. As prices have fallen and fear has spread across the market, bullish commentary has collapsed. XRP now has just 0.61 bullish comments for every bearish one, while Bitcoin stands at around 0.69.

Ethereum is holding up better at around 1.14, but enthusiasm has still fallen sharply from September. These ratios give a clearer picture of when retail traders become unusually confident or fearful, and right now, fear has clearly swept over the crypto community.

Santiment revealed that the darkest sentiment periods have often created the strongest contrarian opportunities once panic has had time to settle. The community is still reeling from crypto’s largest-ever hack, which makes the current situation particularly difficult. Despite this, if BTC and XRP sentiment stays below 1.0 while prices stop making new lows, a mid-term relief rally could eventually take shape.

“Extreme fear alone does not mark the exact bottom, but fear plus price stabilization has often been a much stronger signal.”

Chayanika has been working as a financial journalist for seven years. A graduate in Political Science and Journalism, her interest lies in regulatory implications with a focus on technological evolution in the crypto realm.

North Korea denies role in $6 billion Binance hack after FBI accusation

Reuters, citing KCNA, reported the denial after the FBI blamed TraderTraitor for stealing more than $6 billion from Binance.

By Liam 'Akiba' Wright Editor-in-Chief • CryptoSlate

01 Kim Yo Jong dismissed US claims linking North Korea to the Binance hack as “absurd rhetoric,” Reuters reported on November 2, citing KCNA. 02 The FBI attributed the theft to TraderTraitor and urged crypto services to block transactions involving listed wallets and derived funds. 03 Investigators observed conversion primarily into ether, while further laundering through DeFi and instant-swap services remained an FBI expectation. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

Kim Yo Jong, sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, dismissed US claims linking the country to the Binance hack as “absurd rhetoric,” Reuters reported on Nov. 2, citing the Korean Central News Agency, or KCNA. The denial disputes the US government's attribution of the theft of more than $6 billion from the cryptocurrency exchange.

The FBI had blamed North Korea's TraderTraitor operation in an Oct. 31 alert, placing the theft on or about Oct. 29. TraderTraitor is the bureau's name for the specific North Korean cyber activity it identified in the attack.

Related Reading FBI blames North Korea for $6 billion Binance hack, urges THORChain to block stolen funds

Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs estimated that approximately $6 billion left Binance wallets across ten blockchains, with most of the funds moving in about 20 minutes beginning at 20:05 UTC on Oct. 29. The firm's initial figures reflected observations through 00:30 UTC on Oct. 30.

TRM attributed the Binance hack to TraderTraitor with high confidence, citing on-chain and off-chain intelligence.

The firm also assessed that valid signed transfers across different blockchains pointed to a compromise of Binance's hot-wallet signing infrastructure. That would place the breach in the systems used to authorize outgoing wallet transactions. The explanation remains TRM's assessment of how the transfers were enabled. Its conclusion connects the ability to produce valid transfers on different networks with a potential weakness in the infrastructure used to sign those transactions.

FBI seeks to block transactions linked to the Binance hack

The FBI said investigators working with the US Secret Service and IRS Criminal Investigation had observed the actors converting stolen assets primarily into ether. The bureau expected further laundering through decentralized finance, or DeFi, and instant-swap services.

Related Reading Binance hackers deploy never-seen-before laundering tactics to conceal $6.3 billion theft

The alert urged cryptocurrency service providers to block transactions involving the listed theft-linked addresses. posts.summary: Ethereum remains under pressure near $2.3K after its latest recovery failed to reverse the broader downtrend. With the ascending daily channel already lost, attention is shifting toward nearby demand and the liquidation concentrations beneath the market.
posts.summaryVi: Ethereum remains under pressure near $2.3K after its latest recovery failed to reverse the broader downtrend. With the ascending daily channel already lost, attention is shifting toward nearby demand and the liquidation concentrations beneath the market.
posts.content:
Ethereum remains under pressure near $2.3K after its latest recovery failed to reverse the broader downtrend. With the ascending daily channel already lost, attention is shifting toward nearby demand and the liquidation concentrations beneath the market.

The daily chart shows a clear deterioration in Ethereum’s structure following the breakdown below the ascending channel. A subsequent rebound into the $2.44K–$2.52K supply zone was rejected, reinforcing the bearish significance of the broken channel boundary. Since then, ETH has continued to form lower highs and lower lows.

The latest decline produced a sharp wick toward $2.17K, followed by a modest recovery that has struggled to hold above $2.26K. This suggests that buyers are defending the recent lows, but their response has yet to establish a meaningful reversal. The $2.17K–$2.22K region is now an important near-term support area. A sustained break beneath it would expose the psychological $2K level, followed by the broader daily demand zone at approximately $1.82K–$1.98K.

For buyers to improve the outlook, ETH first needs to recover the $2.31K–$2.36K region, where several recent candles consolidated before the latest selloff. However, the more significant barrier remains the $2.44K–$2.52K supply zone. Until that area is reclaimed, recoveries remain vulnerable to renewed selling.

On the four-hour timeframe, Ethereum continues to trade within a descending channel. The recent selloff reached the $2.17K–$2.22K demand zone near the channel’s lower boundary, triggering a rebound toward $2.31K. That recovery was subsequently rejected, leaving the price back around $2.25K.

The failure to sustain the bounce preserves the sequence of lower highs and suggests that sellers remain in control of the short-term structure. Another test of the $2.17K–$2.22K support zone appears plausible if ETH cannot regain the $2.30K–$2.31K area. Repeated pressure on this demand zone could increase the risk of a breakdown, although the recent rejection wick shows that buying interest is still present.

Alternatively, a sustained recovery above $2.31K would bring the descending channel’s upper boundary, currently around $2.35K–$2.38K, into focus. Breaking that trendline would weaken the immediate bearish setup and could allow a broader recovery toward the $2.44K–$2.52K supply zone.

The Binance ETH/USDT liquidation heatmap highlights estimated liquidation concentrations below the current price. A nearby band sits around $2.15K–$2.20K, broadly overlapping the support region identified on the price charts. A larger, brighter concentration is visible around $2K–$2.05K.

This positioning makes the area just above $2K particularly relevant if Ethereum loses its recent lows. A move into these levels could trigger long liquidations and amplify downside volatility. However, the heatmap identifies potential liquidation exposure rather than guaranteed price targets or confirmed buying support.

Above the market, substantial concentrations remain around $2.8K–$3K, but these are distant from the current structure. For now, the nearby downside clusters and repeated failed recoveries keep the focus on support. A recovery above the four-hour descending channel would be the first technical development to ease that pressure.

posts.content:

Written by Yohan Yun staff editor Edited by Andrew Fenton staff editor Written by Yohan Yun staff editor Edited by Andrew Fenton staff editor

Wall Street killed Bitcoin’s wild rallies: 10x’s Markus Thielen

Magazine Published Nov 3, 2026 Markus Thielen sees Bitcoin reaching $90,000 by year-end, questions institutional ETF demand and says Ethereum must do more for holders.

Bitcoin’s days of consecutive double-digit price surges are over as Wall Street traders and profit-taking whales reshape the market, according to 10x Research founder Markus Thielen.

Institutional traders selling call options after rallies have made Bitcoin’s violent price explosions of earlier years less common, Thielen says in the latest episode of Cointelegraph’s Trade Secrets .

Thielen is also the author of Crypto Titans , a history of the industry. Writing the book led him to notice how each cycle brought different people pitching crypto to investors.

“Every cycle had actually different promoters, and different promoters bring in different investors,” he says.

This time, the promoters come from Wall Street, where investors trade on economic data and Federal Reserve decisions. Thielen says he expects Bitcoin will rise quickly on news, then spend time crab walking across the chart before the next big macro event.

Thielen estimates that market makers account for up to half of the $60 billion in net spot Bitcoin ETF inflows he analyzed. Those firms hold ETF shares as a way to hedge their options trades, so the positions do not necessarily represent a bet that Bitcoin’s price will rise.

“So in the end it was not outright buying,” he says.

His estimate draws on a review of Form 13F filings, which disclose certain securities holdings of investment managers.

Cumulative net inflows into US spot Bitcoin ETFs. Source: Coinglass

Thielen says the first wave of funds into the ETFs also included retail investors buying through institutions and corporate vehicles. Some paid substantial premiums to the value of the underlying crypto holdings.

“I would still think the institutions could come. I would still think that some of the sovereign wealth funds could come,” Thielen says.

Thielen still sees Bitcoin reaching $90,000 by year-end. He says a drop into the mid-to-high $70,000s could come first.

Bitcoin has already been trading in that range, falling to about $76,100 on Friday following Binance’s $6.3 billion hack . BTC finished October down 7.3%, according to Coinglass .

Thielen compares the recovery in prices over recent months with early 2023, when Bitcoin rose from around $20,000 to $30,000. He says the doubts surrounding this year’s rebound are familiar as investors scan for the next price drop and entry point.

BTC’s return to $90,000 may rest partly on how much further the Fed raises borrowing rates. The central bank increased its benchmark rate by a quarter of a percentage point in September, to a target range of 3.75%–4%.

It held rates steady last Wednesday in a split vote, with two officials voting for another quarter-point increase. The Fed’s statement said inflation was still elevated, leaving open the possibility of further increases.

Thielen expects another hike by December, followed by a more cautious approach to further increases that could help Bitcoin rally toward year-end.

Thielen expects Bitcoin to outperform Ether, saying too much of the value from Ethereum activity goes to layer-2 networks.

Making those networks cheaper to use has been a deliberate part of Ethereum’s development. But cheaper transactions may muddy the investment pitch for ETH.

Ethereum burns base fees paid by users, removing those coins from circulation. Its supply shrinks when the amount burned exceeds new ETH issued to validators. Lower fees can mean less ETH is destroyed.

ETH supply grows when issuance exceeds the amount burned. Source: ultrasound.money

Thielen, who says he has been bearish on Ether for more than a year, compares Ethereum with a highway.

“Everybody wants the highway to be empty so you can go fast, and the roads need to be super, super clean and fixed and everything, but nobody wants to pay for it,” he says.

He singles out Hyperliquid as an example of how trading activity can fund token purchases. The decentralized perpetuals exchange’s assistance fund converts trading fees into HYPE, which is then burned.

For Ethereum, he wants a stronger connection between the network’s use and the financial benefit to holders.

Written by Nate Kostar staff writer Edited by Ana Paula Pereira staff editor Written by Nate Kostar staff writer Edited by Ana Paula Pereira staff editor

Binance traces $6.3B hack to fake job interviews, compromised AI tool

Latest News Published Nov 3, 2026 Hackers exploited compromised employee computers and stolen credentials to breach Binance’s wallet infrastructure, according to the exchange’s investigation.

A coding assignment from a prospective employer seemed like an ordinary part of a job interview. Instead, it was one step in a months-long cyberattack that ended with $6.3 billion stolen from Binance, raising questions about how exchanges protect themselves against threats that target their employees.

The attack was part of a coordinated campaign that exploited both human vulnerabilities and internal security systems, according to a postmortem released by Binance on Tuesday. The exchange’s findings detailed how hackers gradually gained access to its wallet infrastructure before the Oct. 29 theft.

According to Binance’s security report, the attack campaign began in June, when an engineer downloaded a tampered software package while setting up an AI coding tool. Although Binance detected the malware and replaced the affected device, the attackers had already gathered information about the exchange’s wallet team.

In September, attackers posing as recruiters targeted another software engineer and tricked the employee into downloading a malicious file disguised as a coding assignment. The malware compromised the engineer’s work computer and evaded the exchange’s security protections.

On Oct. 20, the attackers used the compromised computer and an internal AI tool to gain access to two additional engineers’s systems, obtaining deployment credentials that allowed them to install malicious software within Binance’s wallet infrastructure on Oct. 29.

The attackers then gained access to the exchange’s internal wallet-signing service, which authorizes cryptocurrency transactions. This allowed them to move funds outside the normal withdrawal process.

“This wasn’t one mistake or one breach — it was a months-long campaign,” Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said in a Tuesday post on X.

Binance said the attackers also exploited Ethereum’s EIP-7702 mechanism, which allows wallets to delegate transaction permissions to smart contracts, enabling unauthorized transfers to continue even after the exchange suspended withdrawals. Its multiparty computation (MPC) wallet system, which distributes control over transaction signing, complicated efforts to revoke those permissions.

The breach affected approximately $6.3 billion in digital assets , with Binance reporting that $2.85 billion had been frozen or intercepted, according to its latest accounting. The attack was part of a coordinated campaign that exploited both human vulnerabilities and internal security systems, according to a postmortem released by Binance on Tuesday. The exchange’s findings detailed how hackers gradually gained access to its wallet infrastructure before the Oct. 29 theft.

Hong Kong bank pilot opens 24/7 cash settlement for tokenized fund deals

Participating institutions can settle tokenized deposit transactions in central bank money beyond conventional hours, supporting treasury and fund activity.

By Liam 'Akiba' Wright Editor-in-Chief • CryptoSlate

01 EnsembleTX now supports 24/7 interbank settlement of tokenized deposit transactions in tokenized central bank money. 02 The controlled pilot involves 12 banks and 20 industry pioneers, with access dependent on participating institutions. 03 Trials involving regulated stablecoins remain forthcoming, separate from the upgraded settlement capability already available within the EnsembleTX pilot. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

Hong Kong's tokenization pilot now lets participating banks settle tokenized deposit transactions around the clock in central bank money, extending the cash settlement behind corporate treasury and tokenized-fund activity beyond conventional operating hours.

The Hong Kong Monetary Authority announced the upgrade on Nov. 2. EnsembleTX, the pilot phase of Project Ensemble, now has 12 participating banks and 20 industry pioneers.

The customer deposits and the settlement money have different roles. Participating firms use tokenized deposits supplied by commercial banks; tokenized central bank money settles the transactions between banks. The upgrade extends the hours available for that interbank cash settlement.

Related Reading Central banks map their role in a payments system shared with stablecoins

Participating industry pioneers have already used bank-provided tokenized deposits for corporate treasury management and tokenized money market fund transactions. HKMA names Ant International, BlackRock and China Asset Management (Hong Kong) among the firms involved.

Banks providing tokenized deposits for the cited activity include Bank of China (Hong Kong), China Construction Bank (Asia), ICBC (Asia), Standard Chartered Bank (Hong Kong) and HSBC. These are examples given by HKMA, rather than the full roster of 12 participating banks.

For a corporate treasury using the pilot, the practical change is that its participating bank can settle the relevant transactions outside conventional operating hours. Tokenized-fund users gain extended cash-settlement availability where their banks and platforms support the activity.

Securities and Futures Commission Chief Executive Julia Leung said the capability supports round-the-clock corporate treasury transactions and secondary trading of tokenized funds on licensed platforms. Availability for an individual fund still depends on the bank and platform arrangements; continuous interbank settlement does not establish continuous trading for every fund.

EnsembleTX initially used HKD RTGS. Around-the-clock settlement in tokenized central bank money was a future enhancement.

The change extends interbank settlement hours within a controlled pilot; bank deposits and central bank settlement money keep different roles.

Pilot participants only. Fund trading depends on bank and platform access. The diagram implies no transaction volumes or cost savings.

HKMA settlement upgrade, November 2, 2026 Official EnsembleTX launch, November 13, 2025 Supporting facts

HKMA announced on November 2, 2026 that EnsembleTX supports interbank settlement of tokenized deposit transactions in tokenized central bank money on a 24/7 basis. [1] EnsembleTX launched on November 13, 2025 as a controlled pilot for real-value transactions involving tokenized deposits and digital assets. [2] EnsembleTX initially used the Hong Kong dollar Real Time Gross Settlement system for interbank settlement of tokenized deposit transactions. [1] [2] Participating industry pioneers have used tokenized deposits provided by banks for corporate treasury management and tokenized money market fund transactions. [1] The operational change concerns the interbank settlement route for tokenized deposits within EnsembleTX's participating institutions; it does not establish universal access to a round-the-clock bank service. [1] [2] The releases distinguish tokenized deposits provided by participating commercial banks from the tokenized central bank money used for interbank settlement. [1] [2] For participating treasury and tokenized-fund users, the upgrade makes the interbank cash-settlement component available outside conventional operating hours, subject to the pilot and relevant platform access. [1] [2] Method

Schematic of functional roles, not a transaction sequence or ledger architecture. Banks A and B are illustrative participating banks. Compare the historical RTGS route with the capability announced November 2, 2026; no numerical operating-hours baseline is assumed.

Pilot participants only. Fund trading depends on bank and platform access. The diagram implies no transaction volumes or cost savings.

EnsembleTX launched in November 2025 as a controlled environment for real-value transactions involving tokenized deposits and digital assets. It initially used the Hong Kong dollar Real Time Gross Settlement system. Round-the-clock settlement in tokenized central bank money was envisaged as a later enhancement. November's change extends the settlement infrastructure behind that existing real-value activity.

The newly enabled capability remains within that participating-institution pilot.

HKMA also outlined separate trial work in its FinTech Week update . It reported completed trial trades involving recognized dealers conducting secondary-market transactions in tokenized Exchange Fund Bills, then said it would soon expand trials to include regulated stablecoins.

The planned stablecoin trials remain a separate next step.
